text.p: Following are highlights of the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- State and public services employees get a 10-percent pay rise from July 1. Another three percent increase due in October.
- Trial of Bosnian Croat Tihomir Blaskic for alleged war crimes continues in the Hague. Will the tribunal allow Croatia to try people indicted for war crimes?
- Commentary: Tudjman-Izetbegovic meeting postponed due to obstacles created by the Bosnian side.
- Tourist association opens offices in Vienna, Budapest and London to help promote tourism. Croatia could earn up to $5 billion a year from tourism with careful develpment, says Minister Niko Bulic.
- Ericsson Nikola Tesla had a record 80 million kuna profit on income of almost one billion kuna in 1996.
- Japanese delegation visits the state investment promotion agency (HAPU) to inquire about labour costs, taxation and privatisation of utilities.
- Hundreds of fans meet David Bowie upon arrival in Zagreb, where he will give a concert on Tuesday at the sports hall.
- Where to exchange hard currency in Croatia: Istarska and Dubrovacka Banka offer better rates than Zagreabacka Banka and Bank Austria. Small exchange offices most favourable.
- Croatia Airlines cuts tariffs to the coast from July 1, making it possible to fly to Dubrovnik from Zagreb for no more than 200 kuna one way.
- Interview with Michael Steiner, outgoing U.N. high representative for civilian affairs in Bosnia: The Bosnian Federation is progressing significantly.
- Big fire on the island of Hvar contained.

- Talks are under way to make hotels on the Brijuni Island part of the Intercontinental Hotel corporation, says Zlatko Novak, chief executive of Zagreb's Intercontinental Hotel. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4551840
